title: The Fake Tryouts
premise: Felix Nakamura, a self-erasing statistician at Ridgemont High, notices the varsity basketball tryout roster was decided before anyone tried out—rigged by Coach Voss and a booster with money on every game. When a group chat called The Fake Tryouts begins sending messages that predict events days before they happen, Felix and four misfit classmates realize one of them is somehow seeing the future—or fabricating it. As the predictions turn darker and point to a catastrophic final game, Felix must choose between protecting his only friends and exposing a truth that will burn down the school's beloved season. In the end, Felix testifies, the ring collapses, and he walks into graduation no longer invisible, having learned that identity is something you claim, not something you're assigned.
about_author: Quentin Galloway is a former high school scorekeeper who spent three seasons watching games from behind a clipboard before writing about the kids nobody cheers for. He lives in the Pacific Northwest, where he still keeps meticulous stats for pickup games nobody asked him to track.

chapters.title: The Clipboard Kid
chapters.summary: Felix Nakamura's POV. Felix catalogs Ridgemont High in spreadsheets—who sits where, who matters, who doesn't—and places himself firmly in the invisible column. Establishes his ritual of counting days to graduation. Emotional beat: comfortable numbness masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Numbers Don't Lie, People Do
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. While entering tryout data, Felix finds the final roster timestamped two days before tryouts occurred. He says nothing, filing it away like evidence. Emotional beat: first crack in his safe detachment; curiosity outweighs fear.

chapters.title: Five Strangers in Detention
chapters.summary: Rotating POV introduces Priya (debate captain), Marcus (benched star), Dee (school paper editor), and Theo (Felix's lab partner). All five land in detention for separate small rebellions. Emotional beat: reluctant connection forming among kids who've each been labeled wrongly.

chapters.title: The First Message
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. An unknown group chat named 'The Fake Tryouts' adds all five, predicting the fire alarm will go off during third period Wednesday. It does, precisely at 10:47. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: Group scene, alternating POVs. The five compare notes: each received one prediction before being added. They agree to test the chat with a controlled experiment. Emotional beat: wary alliance; the thrill of belonging to something secret.

chapters.title: The Booster
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus reveals his father owes money to Dale Pruitt, the booster whose donations built the new gym, and admits he was told to shave points this season. Emotional beat: shame and the crushing weight of family loyalty.

chapters.title: Prediction: Rain of Glass
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat predicts a car accident in the faculty lot; it happens, injuring no one but shaking everyone. Priya starts keeping her own ledger of messages versus outcomes. Emotional beat: dread replacing wonder as patterns emerge.

chapters.title: Who Added Us?
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee traces the account through school servers and hits a wall: the chat was created from a device inside the athletic office. Emotional beat: paranoia—the watcher may be watched.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses he transferred schools after being outed, and that invisibility is a survival skill he recognizes in Felix. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; the theme of chosen identity surfaces.

chapters.title: The Second Roster
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A new prediction names which players will 'mysteriously' fail eligibility checks before playoffs—all five targets are kids who refused Pruitt's offers. Felix realizes the chat knows the rigging from the inside. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Coach Voss's Office
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus confronts Voss, who deflects but lets slip he also receives predictions. Marcus realizes the coach is both perpetrator and hostage. Emotional beat: disillusionment with an adult hero.

chapters.title: Split Decisions
chapters.summary: Group scene. Priya wants to go public; Felix argues they need proof; Dee wants to publish without sources; Theo votes silence. The alliance fractures. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth—the central tension made explicit.

chapters.title: What Felix Knew
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Dee discovers Felix sat on the rigged-roster evidence since chapter two and calls him a coward. Felix's invisibility strategy is exposed as complicity. Emotional beat: shame detonating into self-examination.

chapters.title: The Prediction About Me
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The chat sends a private message predicting Felix will betray his friends before the last game. He tells no one. Emotional beat: isolation deepening; fear of a self-fulfilling prophecy.

chapters.title: Pruitt Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Pruitt offers to erase Marcus's father's debt if Marcus delivers the group chat's members' names. Marcus photographs the offer instead. Emotional beat: courage born from desperation.

chapters.title: Unmasked
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo decrypts the device signature: the chat runs on Coach Voss's old laptop—but the messages originate from someone feeding Voss information. The five realize there's a sixth member who's been among them. Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation colliding.

chapters.title: The Sixth Member
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Confrontation reveals it's Assistant Principal Hargrove, a former player Pruitt ruined, who's been using leaked schedules to force exposure of the ring—using the five as pawns. Emotional beat: anger at being manipulated by another person's unfinished story.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. The chat predicts a 'career-ending incident' in the fourth quarter of the championship. The five split: Marcus warns the targeted player, Dee streams live, Priya confronts Pruitt courtside, Theo cuts the gym's network, and Felix walks to the scorer's table with his spreadsheets. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix presents the timestamps, rosters, and ledgers to the state athletics board, speaking publicly for the first time in his life. Pruitt is suspended pending investigation; Voss resigns. Emotional beat: the quiet triumph of a voice finally used.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Group scene. Hargrove faces consequences too, and the five argue about whether the ends excused him. Marcus's father takes accountability; Dee publishes everything, names included. Emotional beat: bittersweet reckoning—truth won, but not cleanly.

chapters.title: Off the Record
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix deletes his graduation countdown spreadsheet and archives the group chat instead—not the predictions, but the five friends' conversations. Emotional beat: tenderness; choosing memory over escape.

chapters.title: Tryouts, For Real
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Felix's POV. At graduation, the five exchange gifts: Marcus gives Felix a jersey with no number, saying labels come off now. Felix steps forward when his name is called, loud and unhidden. Emotional beat: earned hope—an identity claimed, not assigned.
